All teams ↗

Keep the evidence with the conversation

A campaign review often starts with a spreadsheet, continues in a dashboard, and ends in a Slack thread full of explanations that never make it back into the report. A launch has the same problem. The brief sits in one place, customer language in another, and the final call on claims or timing happens in chat.

Maia can prepare the work around those decisions. Give it an approved export, a launch brief, selected research, or access to an app your team has connected. Ask for a campaign table, a customer-language digest, or a launch plan. Maia returns the result to the channel where the people responsible for the decision can question it together.

Start with a campaign review

Choose one campaign and define the comparison before asking for analysis. Supply the reporting period, approved targets, metric definitions, and the report or export that contains the results. Ask Maia to cite the source for each number and label any explanation that the data does not prove.

The output should be easy to inspect in Slack. A useful review shows performance against target, the few changes that cross your team's materiality threshold, and questions for the campaign owner. If attribution windows differ or a source is stale, the brief should say so. The marketer still decides whether to adjust spend, change creative, investigate the data, or leave the campaign alone.

Turn customer language into usable input

Product positioning improves when marketers can see the words customers use, but the source material may be scattered across approved call notes, support cases, research documents, and CRM notes. Start with a defined set of records and a specific question, such as objections raised during evaluation or phrases customers use for a recurring problem.

Ask Maia to group repeated language and preserve a link or citation for every example. The result can separate common themes, minority views, and unanswered questions. That gives the team a research artifact it can challenge. It does not turn a small sample into market truth, and it leaves message choices with the people who own the positioning.

Prepare launches in the channel

For a launch, provide the final brief, approved positioning, target audience, required assets, and the date or dependency plan. Maia can draft a channel plan with owners, open questions, and missing approvals. It can also adapt a final source asset into draft email, social, enablement, or landing-page copy for review.

Keep publishing separate from drafting. A completed copy package is useful on its own. If your setup allows Maia to propose a task or another external change, the exact action should remain visible for approval. Your team owns the claims, budget, audience, timing, and final publication.

Make recurring work specific

Scheduled work is most useful when the rule is narrow. Ask for a Monday report using a named export, fixed date range, agreed targets, and a short list of exceptions. Maia can post the same structured review each week, while the thread holds corrections and decisions the team may want to reuse as guidance.

Do not begin with every channel and every data source. One campaign report gives you a clear way to check the numbers, citations, freshness, and audience. Add customer research or launch coordination after the first workflow produces a brief the team trusts enough to review.

Connect only the sources you need

Each marketer can work with files and apps they are allowed to use. Connection availability depends on your Maia setup, so begin with a supplied export when a live source has not been confirmed. Access to a record also does not decide who should see it in a channel. Choose the channel audience with the underlying information in mind.

Start with one campaign whose targets and results the team already knows. Ask Maia for the weekly review, then resolve a missing explanation or conflicting figure in the channel. The corrected brief becomes the format for the next reporting cycle.

Questions from marketing teams

Can Maia read our CRM or marketing platform?

Maia can work with connected apps and supplied files, subject to the access available in your setup. Confirm the exact system and read operation before building a recurring report around it.

Can Maia pause a campaign or publish content?

Start with analysis and drafts. Any external change needs a supported connection and a visible approval step. The campaign owner should review the proposed action, audience, and timing.

How does Maia apply our brand guidance?

Give Maia the current approved guidance and a final source asset. Ask it to follow named rules and call out conflicts. A marketer still edits and approves the copy before publication.
